The Minnesota State Fair. 12 days of fantastic rides, any food you can think of deep fried and on a stick, unlimited milk for 1 dollar, plenty of livestock and cute animals- CHS miracle of birth center is my favorite, entertaining and educational booths, and tons of other attractions. MoRoots is probably my favorite festival. It's a smaller festival, and features artists from Missouri. It's only been around for a couple of years, but overall, it has had a great lineup and turnout with great bands (Aaron Kamm and the One Drops, The Hooten Hallers, Moon Jr, LuSiD, etc). I know the guy who threw it together, and he's been to festivals of just about every kind, and did this one based on how he thought it should be. There was a good assortment of vendors, and it was very walkable. Music in the day was bluegrass, jam bands, reggae, etc. and at night, it was mainly EDM stuff - a good variety.

Price wasn't too bad either (around $60, I think); it wasn't like the larger fests like Coachella, Wakarusa, EDC, or anything like that where the price is outrageously high that it only allows trustafarians in. By keeping a lower price, it allows a more diverse group of people (families, old hippies, young hippies, college kids, locals, etc.) and thus a more well-rounded experience. Dancing in the crowd, I saw more and more familiar faces as it went on, and that was really nice.

Food vendor prices were really good, too. I am going back next year FOR SURE.

Carolina Rebellion is so far my favorite music fest. Not only is it great music for two days, but it's in one of the least hostile crowds I've ever been a part of. I went to the first one, which was only a day long, but I fell in love. The heat was insane and they were charging a lot for water 8 bucks I think. So I sent up a $20 bill through a train of peoples hands up to the front. I received both my drink and exact change from the same snake action. Which surprised me, because when you are dying for a drink you might be tempted to take someones money. I wouldn't have cared too much because I expected it and sometimes someone not dehydrating is more important than my money, but it was awesome everyone was doing their best to maintain that trust barrier.

And then I went to this past years Rebellion because Slayer. Huge crowds, hundreds of crowd surfers and a great atmosphere. The entire time I only encountered one complete dick weasel. But that was over cast by a sexy girl hanging out with me at the front of the crowd during Manson and Rise Against. If someone got hurt, the crowd would stop moshing, and split to help paramedics get to the person who was hurt. No one was belligerent and no one was an asshole when someone got hurt. People ran around giving away free drinks and pot in the crowds because they just wanted to share the love. It was truly one of the best concerts of my life. And if I can afford it, I will return next year in hopes of a Megadeth or Tool being the main headliner. Slipknot also put on a great show, and I was happy to finally see them. I liked them a lot in highschool, kind of faded from them as my taste grew... well.. better. But I've always wanted to be a part of the Spit It Out crowd jump, and they did it and it was awesome.
